item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 120535
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Sep 11 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula.

Central and Western East Pacific (EP97):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located several hundred miles southwest of the southwestern
coast of Mexico remain disorganized. Environmental conditions are
conducive for development, and a tropical depression is expected to
form over the weekend while it moves generally west-northwestward to
westward over the central and western portions of the eastern
Pacific basin. For more information, including gale warnings, please
see the High Seas Forecast issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad trough of low pressure located several hundred miles
southeast of Hilo, Hawaii is producing disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Gradual development of this system is possible during
the next few days while it moves generally northwestward and then
meanders.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.description: ...NORBERT WEAKENS SLIGHTLY... As of 11:00 PM HST Fri Sep 11 the center of Norbert was located near 17.1, -127.4 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 999 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 60 mph.

item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 120849
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026
 
...NORBERT WEAKENS SLIGHTLY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 127.4W
ABOUT 1205 MI...1935 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1820 MI...2930 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 127.4 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this
general motion is expected to continue over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual strengthening is forecast during the next 48 hours, and
Norbert is forecast to approach hurricane intensity by this weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 120849
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026
 
Deep convection associated with an earlier well-established curved 
band has deteriorated over the past several hours, likely due to 
some mid-level dry air entrainment. A 0442 UTC scatterometer pass 
indicated peak winds just above 40 kt within the northwest quadrant. 
Additionally, the latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from 
TAFB is T3.0/45 kt, with objective estimates from UW-CIMSS ranging 
from 45 to 50 kt. Given these data and the degraded convective 
structure, the initial intensity is lowered to a generous 50 kt.

The initial motion is west-northwestward, or 285/8 kt. The track 
guidance has come into much better agreement this cycle and shows 
Norbert continuing generally westward through the weekend as a low- 
to mid-level subtropical ridge remains north of the cyclone. A 
gradual turn toward the west-southwest is then forecast during the 
early to middle portion of next week. Despite the improved agreement 
among the track guidance this cycle, there has been considerable 
run-to-run variability, and confidence in the forecast beyond the 
weekend remains lower than normal. The NHC track forecast is largely 
an update of the previous advisory and lies close to the multi-model 
consensus (HCCA) and Google DeepMind ensemble mean.

Environmental conditions remain favorable for some strengthening 
over the weekend, and Norbert is forecast to approach hurricane 
intensity by 24 to 36 h. Thereafter, a gradual weakening trend is 
forecast through the remainder of the period, likely due to a 
combination of mid-level dry air entrainment and weakening 
upper-level divergence. Simulated satellite imagery from both the 
GFS and ECMWF broadly support this and depict Norbert struggling to 
maintain organized deep convection as it moves westward to 
west-southwestward next week. The latest NHC intensity forecast has 
been lowered slightly from the previous advisory. It remains above 
the intensity guidance envelope through the weekend, then trends 
toward the middle to upper end of the guidance next week.
